panel.summary: The CI-arm loop has no `stalled`-style safety net for the same fixer-failure shape the panel just added one for
panel.evidence: agent-review-panel.yml gained `needs.fix.result == 'failure'` precisely because "claude-code-action refusing a bot-initiated run" leaves no fix pushed and no fresh cycle. The identical failure mode exists in agent-iterate-ci.yml's single `iterate` job (the `Run Claude Code` step at line 147): if the action refuses or errors, the job reds and nothing comments or labels the PR. The only backstop there is the MAX_ATTEMPTS guard, which counts *failed CI runs* (line 90-93) — and a failed *iterate* run produces no new CI run, so the counter never advances and the loop stalls silently until a human notices.
panel.finding_key: .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml::the ci-arm loop has no `stalled`-style safety net for the same fixer-failure shape the panel just added one for

coderabbit.summary: Make the stalled notification match all failure modes.
coderabbit.detail: **Make the stalled notification match all failure modes.** With `fix` failures now entering this job, Line 479 can report that the review panel failed and produced no verdicts even when the panel succeeded and only the fixer failed. Use a generic pipeline-stalled message or select the message based on which dependency failed.
coderabbit.finding_key: .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml::make the stalled notification match all failure modes.
